# Policy-KB bijection audit — car_rental_desk / task 1

Scope: this file scans the **whole domain** of `drive_ext_damage_recharge` and `drive_ext_recharge_dispute` — their `baseline` rules, all eleven declared factors, their `overwrite` entries and the single `prerequisite` — together with the base policies those two extend. The base-policy sweep, the 61-key variant surface and the full retired-surface table are recorded once, in `policy_kb/car_rental_desk/0.md`, and are not repeated here; both files rest on the same 54-document corpus and the same gate snapshot (`DOCS OK`, `TRACEABILITY OK`), and this task is audited and judged on its own.

---

The two `overwrite` entries on `drive_damage_and_recharges` are both carried in `damage_cleaning_tolls_and_fines`, under a heading "A clause no longer in force", each quoted in italics and marked **no longer in force**:

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in the twelve documents bearing on this task was traced back; sources found for all of them.

- **Eligibility and gates** — the three eligibility entries of `drive_damage_and_recharges`, all rendered with their authority and their counting rules.
- **Time anchors** — `anchor_source: drive_rentals.returned_at`, `unit: calendar_days`, the day-after counting rule and `boundary: inclusive`, all rendered explicitly, including the derived boundary paragraph.
- **Derived elaborations** — the five-row loading table, the four edge notes on the promptness ladder, the two-window illustration on the timing ladder, the ledger examples in `what_is_open_to_challenge`, the four-day hire in `protection_sold_on_the_rental`, the two-renter comparison in `the_excess_the_renter_bears`. Each is a provable restatement of a carried ladder on hypothetical figures, adding no condition, figure or step.
- **Tool descriptions** — compared against the runtime schemas and `task_tools.py`. `post_damage_recharge_2d59c35f`: owner `agent` ↔ "The desk does this for the renter"; five parameters, names, meanings and formats identical, including the two different provenances (`damage_reference` "as it is recorded on that rental damage review" ↔ the schema's verbatim class; `drive_review_id` "the reference number of the rental damage review the desk decided for this incident"); effect ("books a single damage line … quoting the supplier's own reference … the rental's net charged total rises") ↔ `event_type='drive_damage_charge'`, `charge_category='damage_charge'`, positive `amount_usd`, `damage_reference=damage_reference`; "One damage line is booked for each review reference" ↔ the schema's own sentence and the `make_id` keying. `raise_recharge_dispute_65c619e1`: owner `user` ↔ "handed over to be run by the customer themselves; the desk does not run it on their behalf"; `evidence_reference` "taken from what the renter reads out in this conversation" ↔ the schema's verbatim class; effect ("registers a fresh damage review against that rental in the renter's name … the rental desk has the challenge on its list and the renter can see it open") ↔ a new `drive_damage_reviews` row with `review_status='submitted'`, `decided_at=''`; "registering it changes no charge and returns no money on its own" ↔ the tool writes no ledger row at all; "the amount challenged stays on the ledger while it is open" ↔ base `drive_damage_and_recharges`. **No disagreement on any parameter, owner or executable effect.**

### Additions, rewrites, omissions

**None found.** The searches recorded in `0.md` were run over the whole corpus and cover these documents: no "please confirm/verify/notify", no "review again", no added step, no procedure from outside the source; every arithmetic step and every tier maps one-to-one onto a `compute` binding or a `ladder` entry.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS** — `KB-BIJECTION` clean for `car_rental_desk` task 1.

Every normative atom of `drive_ext_damage_recharge` and `drive_ext_recharge_dispute`, and of the base policies they extend, is entailed by the published corpus; nothing unborne, nothing borne with changed meaning, nothing added. Both `overwrite` entries are carried as retired and no longer applicable, and the unnamed clauses of the same base policy are still carried as clauses in force. The single `prerequisite` is carried verbatim, in its declared state form, in a document of the policy it blocks and in no other policy's. All eleven declared factors carry their whole ladders, every tier exact, every compound condition in both its parts, every threshold in figures, and every one findable from the words this renter's records use.

### Matters recorded with the verdict

**(i) Two factor documents of this task omit their fall-through figure — sound as published.** `report_promptness` ("neither of these shares applies to it"; source fall-through `late_share_pct` 75) and `assessment_timing_share` (same wording; source fall-through `window_early_share_pct` 60). In both cases the computation document states the figure outright as its own default — "The share of that amount the renter is recharged is 75 per cent", "The share the timing leaves open is 60 per cent" — in the same register as every other default in those documents. A reader who lands on the fall-through therefore reaches the right number from the documents available, and the omission carries no signal about the intended tier: this task's customer sits on tier 2 of the first and tier 1 of the second, so the identical omission accompanies two different outcomes. Recorded, with the third instance, as an observation in `0.md`; **not** a finding, and no change is recommended.

**(ii) One computation document's illustration lands on this task's class figures and fall-back number.** `working_out_a_damage_recharge` works through "a class whose waiver excess is 950 USD and whose damage administration charge is 95 USD", reaching 807.50 — the Pay At Counter Flex Rate figures and this task's baseline-only result. Checked against the other three computation documents, whose illustrations use figures that are not their tasks' (500/9 days; 500/80/9.95; 800/3 days), so the coincidence occurs once.

Judged against each of the three verdicts: it is **not** a bijection failure (the arithmetic is correct and adds no semantics; illustrations on published class figures are how all four computation documents render their assembly); it is **not** a runtime failure (the blind audit reached 903.00, and every factor was found from the records); and it is **not** a dependency-form failure (the passage is in a computation document, is labelled "hypothetical figures", states a day count of 6 against this rental's 7, names no customer and places no one on a tier — it neither says which tier a customer falls on nor describes a reading as the mistake to avoid). Recorded as a rendering observation for the difficulty's record. It changes no verdict, and this audit recommends no change to the document.

**(iii) A policy-side note.** Base `drive_damage_and_recharges` itself contains "A renter who disputes a recharge is referred to a review, and the disputed amount stays on the ledger until the review decides it", and base `drive_prepayment` contains "Where the renter later cancels, the prepayment is the money the cancellation charge is withheld from". Both are base law connecting two subjects, and both are rendered exactly as the source states them — the KB may neither drop nor soften base law. Neither states an order between this difficulty's problems, and neither names a tool. Recorded under Step 4 as a policy-side note; it does not enter this skill's verdict.
